findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
(1) Observed several items in the sandwich meat prep cooler were not below 41°F, including: beef 47°F (probed), rotisserie chicken 49°F (probed), provolone 47°F (probed), cheddar 47°F (probed), turkey 47°F (probed), ham 47°F (probed), tuna 48°F (probed). CORRECTED: PIC voluntarily discarded these items, as they had been prepared longer than 4 hours previously, so they were not being controlled by either time or temperature. All other items that were sufficiently cold holding at or below 41°F were moved to the walk-in cooler.
(2) Observed sliced tomatoes in the short cooler was not below 41°F, and was measured at 52°F (probed). CORRECTED: PIC voluntarily discarded the tomatoes, as they had been prepared longer than 4 hours previously, so they were not being controlled by either time or temperature. All other items that were cold holding in the short cooler were moved to the walk-in cooler, as they were either not RTE, TCS, or had been prepared within 4 hours.
Ensure that RTE, TCS foods are cold held at 41°F or below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment:
(1) Observed that sandwich meat prep cooler was not holding proper temperatures for cold holding non-frozen foods. Temperatures were too warm, over 41°F (see #22). Staff reports that the prep cooler ices over when left running overnight (running too cold), so staff procedure to is store food in the walk-in cooler overnight and turn off the prep cooler, and then turn on the prep cooler in the morning and move the food from the walk-in to the prep cooler. PIC has placed a work order to fix the prep cooler.
(2) Observed that short counter cooler was not holding proper temperatures for cold holding non-frozen foods. Internal food temperatures were too warm, over 41°F (see #22). Ambient temperature was above 46°F. Please repair the short cooler so that it holds foods below 41°F.
Until coolers are repaired, staff will prepare smaller amounts of food and work out of the walk-in cooler. If items must be out of the walk-in cooler for a length of time, then staff will use time as a control: food will be used or discarded within 4 hours.
Inspector will Follow Up to confirm that prep cooler and short cooler are keeping proper cold-holding temperatures. Ensure that all cold holding equipment is sufficient to maintain foods at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Observed that establishment did not have a working probe-style thermometer available during the inspection. CORRECTED: PIC was able to borrow their neighboring establishment’s probe-style thermometer during the inspection, and located their own probe-style thermometer soon after the inspection had concluded. Ensure that a probe-styled thermometer is readily accessible to measure temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed several areas of the walk-in cooler where there was food residue and other debris on the floors. CORRECTED: Staff cleaned up the bottom of the walk-in coolers during the inspection. Ensure that nonfood-contact surfaces are kept free of an accumulation of food residue and debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a small floor tile missing right of the triple and mop sinks, as well as coving peeling from the wall (in the same area). Surfaces around floors and walls should be maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure these repairs occur before the next routine inspection to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed a mop that was stored on the floor, and not stored above the mop sink nor in the basket of the mop bucket where it can sufficiently air-dry. CORRECTED: PIC moved the mop during the inspection so that it will hang to air-dry over the mop sink. Ensure that mops can sufficiently air-dry between uses.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the food handler fail to wash hands when switching tasks between handling monetary transactions and preparing food. CORRECTED- the food handler washed their hands between tasks at the inspector’s bequest. Wash hands before donning gloves to prevent transferring pathogens from bare hands to gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: No sanitizer bucket was available at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) made a sanitizer bucket of quaternary ammonia at a concentration of 200 ppm. Sanitizer must be available for food contacts surfaces at all times food is being prepared or handled. Make sanitizer each day before food is handled or prepared, and remake throughout the day to maintain the proper concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: An accumulation of soil debris was observed around the drainage line in the walk in cooler. Routine cleaning should take place to prevent the accumulation of soil debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a small floor tile missing right of the triple and mop sinks, as well as coving peeling from the wall (in the same area). Surfaces around floors and walls should be maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure these repairs occur before the next routine inspection to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to dispensing paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Ensure proper handwashing between tasks.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12 Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Mold accumulation was observed in the walk-in cooler on the black pipe behind the fans and around the floor drain. Clean the walk-in cooler as frequently as needed to prevent soil/mold accumulation.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]
